question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.**

To twiddle one's thumbs
solution:
The correct answer is: **To be idle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom** "to twiddle one's thumbs"** means** to be idle, to do nothing, or to pass the time with no productive activity**. It implies a state of inactivity or waiting without any purposeful engagement.
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• Imagine a situation where someone is waiting for an important phone call, but they have nothing else to do in the meantime. They might say, "I've been **twiddling my thumbs** all morning waiting for that call."
 
• In this example,** "twiddling one's thumbs"** indicates the person's state of being idle or not having anything constructive to occupy their time.
 
 
 
• Among the given alternatives, **option 1) "To be idle"** is the best expression that captures the meaning of the idiom accurately.
